skill.name: docs-sources
skill.description: Guides documentation source discovery, framework detection, fetch strategy selection, and registry configuration across llms.txt, GitHub, API specifications, sitemaps, and browser automation.
skill.summary: Select and configure reliable documentation fetching strategies.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms two medium risks: nested sitemap fetching and browser link navigation can reach attacker-selected destinations. Other alerts are safe examples, Markdown formatting, fixed URLs, localhost checks, or harmless redirection; no prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Nested sitemap URLs are fetched without destination validation.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only HTTP and HTTPS URLs on approved public hosts. Block private, loopback, link-local, and metadata addresses before each request.

remediation.issue: Browser automation follows extracted links without an origin policy.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve every link before navigation, require an approved origin, reject unsafe schemes, and cap pages, depth, redirects, and response size.

content.value_statement: Documentation sites expose content through different platforms and formats. This skill identifies the source type and recommends a practical fetch and registry strategy.
actual_capabilities: Detects documentation frameworks from config files, repository structure, and site signals.
Prioritizes llms.txt, GitHub raw content, API specifications, sitemaps, and browser automation.
Provides targeted fetch and detection commands for common documentation platforms.
Drafts registry configurations with source paths, strategies, priorities, and filters.
Maps common development libraries to likely documentation sources and strategies.
limitations: Does not verify that every example URL remains available.
Browser fetching requires an existing browser wrapper and Chrome debugging setup.
Private repositories and protected APIs require credentials that the skill does not manage.
Remote content can be incomplete, rate-limited, or untrusted.

use_cases.title: Add a documentation source
use_cases.description: Detect the source platform, select a fetch strategy, and prepare a registry entry for a development team.

use_cases.title: Migrate documentation ingestion
use_cases.description: Compare raw repository content, structured specifications, sitemaps, and browser fetching before changing an ingestion pipeline.

use_cases.title: Complete an AI documentation registry
use_cases.description: Match detected project libraries to missing documentation sources and prioritize additions.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a fetch strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze documentation at {url}. Check source signals and recommend one fetch strategy with concise evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Configure one source
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a registry entry for {library} at {url}. Detect its framework and specify the strategy, source paths, priority, and filters.

prompt_templates.title: Compare source options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare llms.txt, repository, API specification, sitemap, and browser options for {project}. Rank them by completeness, reliability, and maintenance cost.

prompt_templates.title: Design a resilient rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a documentation ingestion plan for {projects}. Include detection evidence, primary and fallback strategies, validation controls, rate limits, and registry updates.

output_examples.input: Choose a strategy for a site that publishes llms.txt.
output: Reason: the source is already optimized for language model consumption.
Fallback: use repository content, then a sitemap, if coverage is incomplete.

output_examples.input: Assess documentation built from a public Docusaurus repository.
output: Detection evidence: Docusaurus config and sidebar files are present.
Registry guidance: record the repository, branch, documentation path, and navigation config.

output_examples.input: Plan ingestion for a JavaScript-rendered documentation site.
output: Try llms.txt, repository content, API specifications, and the sitemap first.
Use browser automation only when direct requests return incomplete shell content.
Restrict navigation to approved public origins and apply crawl limits.

best_practices: Check AI-native and raw repository sources before crawling rendered pages.
Validate every remote destination and restrict crawls to approved public origins.
Record detection evidence and test the selected strategy before updating the registry.
anti_patterns: Do not launch browser automation before testing simpler direct-fetch methods.
Do not follow sitemap or page links without scheme, host, and network-range validation.
Do not add registry entries without confirming framework signals and source paths.

faq.question: Which strategy should I try first?
faq.answer: Check for llms.txt first, then repository content, structured API specifications, sitemaps, and browser automation.

faq.question: Can this skill fetch private repositories?
faq.answer: It explains repository strategies, but authentication and credential handling must be configured separately.

faq.question: When is browser automation appropriate?
faq.answer: Use it when direct requests return incomplete content from a JavaScript-rendered site and simpler sources are unavailable.

faq.question: Which documentation frameworks are covered?
faq.answer: The references cover Fern, Docusaurus, MkDocs, Mintlify, Sphinx, Nextra, Starlight, Antora, GitBook, VuePress, and ReadTheDocs.

faq.question: Does the skill create registry entries?
faq.answer: It provides configuration structures and examples. The calling agent must apply and validate the final registry change.

faq.question: How should remote links be handled safely?
faq.answer: Allow approved public HTTP or HTTPS origins, block private network ranges, limit redirects, and cap crawl depth and response size.
